name: Hassophereth
overview: Hassophereth is a male figure mentioned in the Bible as a servant of Solomon. Beyond this unique attribute, Scripture does not provide additional details about his tribe or other personal notes. His role as Solomon's servant places him within the context of the royal administration during Solomon's reign.
namesAndTitles: The name Hassophereth means '(office of) scribes,' indicating a possible connection to the administrative or literary functions in the kingdom. A variant of his name, Sophereth, carries the same meaning and appears in a parallel biblical reference, suggesting consistency in his identity and role as related to scribal duties.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Hassophereth beyond his designation as Solomon's servant. There are no additional familial or relational details provided in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Hassophereth's significance lies in his service under King Solomon, reflecting the organized and structured nature of Solomon's court. His association with the scribal office underscores the importance of record-keeping and administration during this period of Israel's history. Although mentioned briefly, his presence affirms the biblical portrayal of Solomon's governance supported by capable officials.
